annotations.text:
The open decision is this row: where the panel lives.
Everything below works with either.

Docked in the right sidebar.
Obsidian's own place for this, so it survives layout changes and remembers its width. Costs permanent screen width, and it is the third sidebar a person already has open.

Floating over the board.
Costs nothing when shut, opens where the eye already is, and is the shape of a command palette people know. But it covers the board it is editing, and has nowhere to keep a long transcript.
Attaching a tile is what makes a prompt precise. Same gesture as Cursor: select, then ask. The chip shows the scope so nobody has to guess what the answer will touch.
The folder starts under the prompt need no agent — they come from the fields each folder has. This is the law drawn out: the agent is an accelerator, not a dependency.
Phone: the board is fully usable and editable; only the prompt is desktop. The note says so instead of hiding the button.
